narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated an 80% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high predicted risk, so the admissions decision treated you as unlikely to succeed on the licensing exam. The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. That gap pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing was the next most influential factor, and it also pointed toward failure: you were again in the second decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor and also increased the predicted risk; at 2.80 it was below the accepted-student average of about 3.23. Although your LSAT score and family-income background were part of your profile, they were not among the three strongest drivers of this decision. To move forward, ask admissions for specific feedback, meet with an academic advisor about strengthening your record, and consider whether retaking the LSAT or completing additional coursework would make your case more competitive. Focus especially on demonstrating sustained academic improvement, because your class-standing pattern was the clearest concern.
